title: NOT NULL Constraint
description: Learn how to use the NOT NULL constraint to prevent NULL values in a column.

data.text: The NOT NULL constraint specifies that a column must not accept NULL values. By default, if you don't specify NOT NULL, SQL Server allows the column to accept NULL.

data.title: NOT NULL as Column Constraint
data.content: Creates a table with NOT NULL constraints on required columns.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE hr.persons(
    person_id INT IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    last_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    phone VARCHAR(20)
);

data.text: In this example, first_name, last_name, and email cannot be NULL, while phone is optional.
Add NOT NULL to an Existing Column
To add a NOT NULL constraint to an existing column, first update any NULL values, then alter the column:

data.title: Add NOT NULL Constraint
data.content: Updates NULL phone values then adds NOT NULL constraint.

data.text: To remove the NOT NULL constraint, use ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN with NULL:

data.title: Remove NOT NULL Constraint
data.content: Removes the NOT NULL constraint from the phone column.
data.code:
ALTER TABLE hr.persons
ALTER COLUMN phone VARCHAR(20) NULL;

data.title: NOT NULL Key Points
points: NOT NULL prevents NULL values from being inserted or updated in a column.
It is always defined as a column constraint, not a table constraint.
To add NOT NULL to an existing column, first update NULL values.
To remove NOT NULL, use ALTER COLUMN with the NULL keyword.
NOT NULL is different from PRIMARY KEY — PRIMARY KEY implies NOT NULL.
